When in Seattle, this market and Uwajimaya are my go-tos.  Kenji, your grocery shopping energy is invigorating.  It's hard to explain to people, but that sense of excitement and discovery is why I love shopping at the Asian markets.

BTW, I heard the following on NPR on why produce is so cheap at Asian supermarkets - so don't blame me if it's wrong.  According to their reporting, major American supermarket chains only accept produce that has a long remaining shelf life of ~3 weeks.  This is so the produce can wend their way through the market's internal distribution chain and still have decent amount of shelf life.  Apparently the business model of Asian supermarkets is to take produce that is rejected by major chains at a HUGE discount. Because Asian consumer behaviour is same day consumption, produce does not need multi-week shelf life. Also, the purchase cost is so low, that the market can throw away half of the produce and still turn a profit.  Seems accurate to me since I see store workers regularly "prune" bad produce from the display.
